findings.title: Payment for work-in-progress on convenience
findings.deviation: The clause limits payment on convenience termination to 'services rendered', which in this fixed-price context may be interpreted as only completed and accepted milestones.
findings.impact: AtliQ risks not being paid for partially completed work or milestones in progress at the time of termination.
findings.quote: Upon termination by Client for convenience (§ 648 BGB), Supplier shall be entitled to the agreed remuneration for services rendered plus compensation for committed costs.
findings.counterPosition: Supplier shall be entitled to payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs.

findings.title: LDs not specified as sole remedy
findings.deviation: The clause allows for delay penalties to be credited against actual damages rather than being the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
findings.impact: The client could potentially claim additional damages for delay if they exceed the 5% cap.
findings.quote: The contractual penalty shall be credited against any claim for damages for the same delay.
findings.counterPosition: Liquidated damages shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Confidentiality term exceeds playbook standard
findings.deviation: The confidentiality obligation lasts 5 years post-termination, exceeding the preferred 2-3 year window.
findings.impact: AtliQ must maintain internal controls to protect client data for an extended duration after the project ends.
findings.quote: The confidentiality obligation shall continue for five (5) years after termination of this Agreement.
findings.counterPosition: The confidentiality term should be limited to 2–3 years post-termination.

fine.note: Liability is mutually capped at the total contract value, which aligns with the 1x fees standard for this duration.
IP terms correctly protect AtliQ's background IP (PipeKit) and condition delivery of exclusive rights on full payment.
The 30-day payment term is within the 30-45 day playbook standard.
The indemnity is mutual and the IP infringement indemnity matches standard practice.
A DPA is incorporated and liability for data incidents is subject to the general liability cap.
